# v0.4.0 — Device recognition and charging control

This release makes device information easier to read and lets you turn off
the charging-current limit directly in Home Assistant. The minimum remains
**Home Assistant 2026.9.0**.

## Device information

- The default device name is **Mennekes Amtron**. Custom names are preserved.
- Leading underscore padding is removed from displayed serial and article
  numbers, without changing existing device identifiers or entity IDs.
- Article numbers resolve to model names for **13 documented variants** of
  Amtron 4You 300, Compact 2.0s and Start 2.0s, including **4You 310 11 T2S**.
  Unknown articles retain a generic model name and their own article number.

See the [compatibility matrix](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-mennekes-amtron/blob/v0.4.0/docs/compatibility.md)
for the exact variants and manufacturer sources. The owner reported successful
hardware operation of the previous released integration on an **Amtron 4You
310 11 C2**. This does not establish hardware validation of these new changes
or the other listed models.

## Charging-current control

**Charging current limit** is now a number input:

- **0 A turns the EMS limit off.** Hardware limits still apply, but the
  integration's additional current cap is bypassed.
- **6 A or more enables a limit again**, up to the configured maximum.
- Values between 0 and 6 A are rejected. Use **Charging paused** to stop a charge.

Unlimited mode displays as 0 and is remembered across pause/resume and entry
reloads. Active current-control automations can set a new limit again. Direct
`set_charging_current` action calls still require `allow_unlimited: true` for 0.
Error recovery uses the manufacturer's sequence with a limit of at least 6 A;
set 0 again afterward if you want the limit off.

Write intervals and the remembered resume setting now survive entry reloads.
On first setup or a full Home Assistant restart, current writes wait five
seconds and pause/resume/phase changes wait five minutes while timing history
is unknown. Reading and the heartbeat remain available.

Fresh device status is checked before restarting or switching phases. Recovery
checks cooldowns before changing charging release. Delayed readback cannot undo
pause protection, and failed heartbeats retry after one second.

## Database and runtime maintenance

A new **Suggest Recorder exclusions** action suggests exclusions using your actual
entity IDs; it does not change your configuration or history. Timing guards
and runtime diagnostics stay in memory without new periodically changing entity
attributes. The integration does not impose a database size cap; use the
[Recorder guide](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-mennekes-amtron/blob/v0.4.0/docs/recorder.md)
to choose a profile and retention policy.

Continuous tests now combine serial reconnects, delayed replies, heartbeat
timing and real SQLite Recorder purge/repack operations. Release packaging is
isolated and atomic; downloaded assets are verified before publication.
Release jobs install dependencies without shared caches, preventing a moved
tag from supplying cached executables to the publisher.

## Updating

Existing **0.2.x and 0.3.x** entries, entity IDs and automations can be kept.
No entry or blueprint migration is required from 0.3.0. For older versions,
follow the [upgrade instructions](https://github.com/memphi2/ha-mennekes-amtron/blob/v0.4.0/docs/upgrading.md).

One installation archive serves HACS and the Marketplace:
**`ha-mennekes-amtron.zip`**. Checksums, build metadata and an SPDX SBOM accompany
it. The domain remains **`mennekes_amtron_rtu`**. Required validation covers
minimum HA and latest stable HA; preview checks remain separate.
